idea: Simple ways to protect plumbing during renovation
title: Renovation Prep: Shield Your Plumbing From Debris
description: Home renovations generate a lot of drywall dust, tile mortar, and fine debris that can easily compromise your plumbing. Whenever you remove a sink, toilet, or vanity, immediately seal open drain and supply pipes. Installing simple plastic test caps or mechanical expansion plugs over open stub-outs prevents heavy construction dust and tile grout from falling inside, where it can set hard and create severe blockages deep in your drain lines. Additionally, capping open waste pipes keeps foul sewer gas out of your living space. Always keep main shut-off valves clear and accessible throughout the build. Small protective measures today prevent costly pipe jetting tomorrow.
image_prompt: A vertical, eye-level commercial photograph taken inside a residential bathroom undergoing renovation. In sharp focus in the lower-center frame, a clean 2-inch white PVC drain stub-out extends horizontally from a hole cut into cement backer board. The open end of the PVC pipe is securely sealed with a bright red rubber expansion test plug with a silver wing nut tightened at its center. Adjacent to it, two 1/2-inch copper water supply lines protrude cleanly from the wall, each fitted with a bronze solder cap. In the softly blurred background, raw timber framing studs and unpainted drywall show subtle plaster dust texture, capturing an active remodeling project. Natural daylight mixed with ambient interior lighting creates realistic reflections on the smooth plastic, brass, and rough wall surfaces.
